summary: Order-service p99 latency and ledger-db statement timeouts were caused by portfolio-service deployment dep-5905 (v4.5.0) at 08:56:00Z, which added a new query on the 'trades' table filtered by account_id + executed_at with no supporting migration/index. This produced a Seq Scan over a 48.2M-row table (logged by ledger-db as application_name=portfolio-service starting 08:58:38), saturating the shared ledger-db (CPU 30%->96%, connections 62->190, slow_queries_per_min 1->140). The saturated shared database blocked order-service's INSERT INTO orders, causing p99 to jump from ~149ms to ~5300ms at 08:57 and 284 statement-timeout errors from 09:00:42. The reported suspicion (DBA autovacuum change at 08:00) is contradicted by timing: it precedes onset by ~56 minutes with no metric deviation, and the only autovacuum activity logged is routine audit_log processing. Pricing-engine, exchange-gateway, disk, and traffic are all ruled out.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Portfolio-service v4.5.0 deploy added an unindexed seq-scan query on trades, saturating shared ledger-db and stalling order-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deployment dep-5905 (portfolio-service v4.5.0, 08:56) introduced a new query 'SELECT * FROM trades WHERE account_id=$1 AND executed_at > $2 ORDER BY executed_at' with no supporting index/migration. This forced a Seq Scan over a 48.2M-row table, driving ledger-db CPU to ~96%, connections to ~190, and slow_queries_per_min to ~140. The saturated shared ledger-db then delayed order-service INSERT INTO orders past its statement timeout, producing 284 timeout errors and p99 latency of ~5.3s. order-service itself was not released.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5905 deployed to portfolio-service at 08:56 with a new query on trades and no migration/index
New query produces 'Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907)' from application_name=portfolio-service, first seen 08:58:38
Seq scans saturate shared ledger-db: CPU 30->96%, connections 62->190, slow_queries_per_min 1->140
Saturated ledger-db blocks order-service INSERTs; order-service p99 jumps from ~149ms to ~5300ms at 08:57 and 284 statement-timeout errors appear from 09:00:42

assumptions: The deployed query lacks a usable index on trades(account_id, executed_at) — the seq scan plan plus 'no migration included' imply this.
ledger-db resource contention is the mechanism by which order-service INSERTs time out (shared datastore).

ranked_hypotheses.title: DBA autovacuum tuning (cfg-2903) on ledger-db caused the slowdown
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 08:00 config change making autovacuum more aggressive (scale_factor 0.2->0.1) increased I/O/CPU on ledger-db and slowed queries, incidentally affecting order-service.

causal_chain.claim: Metrics stayed flat until 08:57, 56 min later — no plausible causal timing

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The change at 08:00 precedes the 08:57 onset by ~56 minutes, with no latency/CPU/connection deviation in the 08:00-08:54 interval (all metrics flat through 08:36-08:54). The positive link is instead the 08:56 deploy to the exact query/application_name seen in the slow-query logs, and the only autovacuum log activity is routine audit_log processing.

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db infrastructure/resource failure (IOPS throttling or disk exhaustion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: ledger-db suffered an infrastructure/resource fault (e.g. IOPS throttling as in HIST-110 or disk-full as in HIST-114) that degraded it and dragged down order-service.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: disk_used_pct stayed flat ~71% (no disk exhaustion). Slow queries are explicitly attributable to a specific new portfolio-service query doing a Seq Scan, not to generic IO errors. No IOPS/capacity metric shows a fault independent of the query pattern.

facts.statement: order-service p99 was ~150ms until 08:54, jumped to ~1968ms at 08:57 and ~5300ms from 09:00.
The only deployment in the window is dep-5905 (portfolio-service v4.5.0) at 08:56:00Z, adding a new trades query with no migration.
ledger-db slow-query logs show 'Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907)' attributed to application_name=portfolio-service, first at 08:58:38.
ledger-db CPU rose from ~30% to ~96% and slow_queries_per_min from ~1 to ~140 after 08:49.
order-service logged 284 statement-timeout errors on INSERT INTO orders starting 09:00:42.
The autovacuum config change cfg-2903 occurred at 08:00:00Z, ~56 min before onset.
No unusual autovacuum activity on the trades table was logged; only routine audit_log processing.
pricing-engine and exchange-gateway latency and ledger-db disk usage and portfolio-service request rate were all flat.

assumptions: The new portfolio-service query has no usable index on trades(account_id, executed_at); the seq-scan plan and 'no migration included' strongly imply this but no schema dump was retrieved.
ledger-db connection/CPU saturation is the causal mechanism for order-service INSERT delays, inferred from shared datastore usage and correlated timing; no direct lock/queue metrics were available.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back portfolio-service to pre-v4.5.0 (before dep-5905) or disable the new P&L breakdown feature to immediately relieve ledger-db.
recommended_actions.rationale: The deploy introduced the seq-scan query; the serving path recovers once the offending query stops.

recommended_actions.action: Add a composite index on trades(account_id, executed_at) (concurrently) so the new query uses an index scan instead of a 48M-row seq scan.
recommended_actions.rationale: The seq scan is the proven mechanism; an index removes it without removing the feature.

recommended_actions.action: Re-apply the portfolio-service change only after EXPLAIN verification and a migration/index gate.
recommended_actions.rationale: 'no migration included' allowed an unindexed query into a large table; a query-review gate prevents recurrence.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on shared-DB slow_queries_per_min and per-query seq-scan detection, plus per-query cost budget.
recommended_actions.rationale: A shared datastore fault surfaced as latency in an unrelated service; earlier detection shortens time-to-diagnosis.

data_gaps: No schema/index catalog for ledger-db was available, so the presumed missing index on trades(account_id, executed_at) is inferred from the seq-scan plan, not directly confirmed.
No direct lock-wait or per-statement queue metrics on ledger-db; the mechanism linking DB saturation to order-service INSERT timeouts is inferred from correlated timing and shared-datastore topology.
No rollback of dep-5905 has been performed, so the counterfactual (recovery on rollback) is unverified.

portfolio-service request_rate stayed flat ~570 req/s across the window (no traffic surge) and its error_rate stayed ~0.2%.
ledger-db is a shared datastore; order-service uses it as 'db' and portfolio-service reads the same 'trades' table (slow queries tagged application_name=portfolio-service).
